nodes.text: Personal history of • Ulcerative colitis • Crohn’s colitis

footnotes.text: If PSC is present, annual surveillance colonoscopies should be started independent of the individual’s time since symptom onset or colonoscopic findings and instead should be initiated at time of PSC diagnosis. Family history of CRC is another important risk factor for developing CRC in patients with IBD, and such individuals may benefit from earlier initiation of colonoscopic surveillance (Samadder NJ, et al. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019;17:1807-1813; Shergill AK, et al. Gastrointest Endosc Clin N Am 2014;24:469-481).

In patients with either ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease, risk factors for dysplasia include PSC, colonic stricture, family history of CRC (particularly when diagnosed age <50 years), personal history of dysplasia; severe long-standing inflammation; and dense pseudopolyposis. In Crohn’s disease, patients with colitis historically involving more than one third of the colon require increased-risk surveillance. In contrast, patients with isolated small bowel Crohn's disease should follow average-risk screening and surveillance recommendations. In patients with isolated ulcerative proctitis without historical extension of inflammation proximal to the rectum, there is little or no increased risk for CRC compared with the population at large; therefore, consider 5-year follow-up or average-risk follow-up.

Surveillance endoscopy ideally should be performed during quiescent disease in order to optimize endoscopic detection of subtle dysplastic lesions and to avoid false-positive pathology findings of dysplasia. Targeted biopsies improve detection of dysplasia, and should be performed for surveillance colonoscopies in patients with ulcerative colitis. High-definition colonoscopes are suggested. If using standard-definition colonoscopes, non-targeted biopsies in 4 quadrants every 10 cm should be performed and dye spray chromoendoscopy is recommended (Murthy SK, et al. Gastroenterology 2021;161:1043-1051; Picco MF, et al. Inflamm Bowel Dis 2013;19:1913-1920; Laine L, et al. Gastrointest Endosc 2015;81:489-501).

Patients with ulcerative colitis develop sporadic colorectal adenomas at the same rate as the general population. Lesions that appear endoscopically and histologically similar to a sporadic adenoma or SSP/ SSL and without invasive carcinoma in the polyp can be treated safely by polypectomy. Some lesions may require endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) or endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) techniques for complete resection. Confirmation of all polyp histology and dysplasia by an expert GI pathologist is desirable.

footnotes.text: Therapy-associated polyposis is an acquired phenotype that presents years after exposure to chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy.

Germline MGPT should include at minimum the following CRC risk-associated genes: APC, MUTYH, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM, BMPR1A, SMAD4, PTEN, STK11, and TP53. PVs associated with adenomatous polyposis include, but are not limited to, monoallelic PVs in APC, GREM1, POLE, POLD1, and AXIN2, and biallelic PVs in MUTYH, NTHL1, and MSH3.

personal_history_adenoma_or_ssp_ssl.definition: Patient has a personal history of adenoma(s) or sessile serrated polyp/lesion(s) (SSP/SSL).

personal_history_adenoma.definition: Patient has a personal history of adenoma(s).

personal_history_ssp_ssl.definition: Patient has a personal history of sessile serrated polyp(s)/lesion(s) (SSP/SSL).

personal_history_tsa.definition: Patient has a personal history of traditional serrated adenoma(s) (TSA).

personal_history_hyperplastic_polyp_max_.definition: Size of the largest hyperplastic polyp in the patient's personal history, in mm.

personal_history_crc.definition: Patient has a personal history of colorectal cancer (CRC).

personal_history_ibd.definition: Patient has a personal history of inflammatory bowel disease: ulcerative colitis or Crohn colitis.

personal_history_aya_cancer.definition: Patient has a personal history of childhood, adolescent, or young adult cancer.

personal_history_solid_organ_transplant.definition: Patient has a history of solid organ transplant.

personal_history_hereditary_syndrome.definition: Hereditary CRC syndrome or pathogenic variant the patient carries; none if no such diagnosis.

family_history_first_degree_crc.definition: At least one first-degree relative has CRC at any age.

family_history_second_third_degree_crc.definition: At least one second- or third-degree relative has CRC at any age.

youngest_crc_relative_age_at_diagnosis_y.definition: Age at CRC diagnosis of the youngest relative with CRC; blank if no relative has CRC.

first_degree_relative_polyp_size_mm.definition: Largest polyp size in a first-degree relative, in mm.

first_degree_relative_polyp_histology.definition: Most advanced histology of a polyp found in a first-degree relative.

first_degree_relative_polyp_dysplasia_gr.definition: Highest dysplasia grade reported for a polyp found in a first-degree relative.

first_degree_relative_high_grade_dysplas.definition: The case explicitly states that a polyp in a first-degree relative shows high-grade dysplasia.

mmr_status.definition: Mismatch repair status of the tumor.

mgpt_result.definition: Multigene panel testing result for hereditary polyposis and CRC genes.

gi_polyp_lifetime_count.definition: Cumulative number of GI polyps of any type (adenomas, SSP/SSL, hamartomas) over the whole GI tract, lifetime.

aya_received_chemotherapy.definition: Patient received systemic chemotherapy for a childhood, adolescent, or young adult cancer.

aya_received_abdominopelvic_radiation_or.definition: Patient received radiation involving the abdominopelvic field (abdomen, pelvis, spine lumbar/sacral/whole) or total body irradiation, regardless of dose, for a childhood, adolescent, or young adult cancer.

chosen_screening_modality.definition: Screening modality selected for the patient.

polyp_count.definition: Number of polyps found at the current examination.

adenoma_count.definition: Number of adenomas found at the current examination.

ssp_ssl_count.definition: Number of sessile serrated polyps/lesions (SSP/SSL) found at the current examination.

tsa_count.definition: Number of traditional serrated adenomas (TSA) found at the current examination.

hyperplastic_polyp_count.definition: Number of hyperplastic polyps found at the current examination.

adenoma_or_ssp_count.definition: Number of adenomas and SSP/SSL found in a single colonoscopy.

adenoma_or_ssp_cumulative_count.definition: Cumulative number of adenomas and SSP/SSL over all colonoscopies.

largest_polyp_size_mm.definition: Size of the largest polyp found at the current examination, in mm.

largest_adenoma_size_mm.definition: Size of the largest adenoma found, in mm.

largest_ssp_ssl_size_mm.definition: Size of the largest SSP/SSL found, in mm.

largest_tsa_size_mm.definition: Size of the largest TSA found, in mm.

largest_hyperplastic_size_mm.definition: Size of the largest hyperplastic polyp found, in mm.

adenoma_villous_or_tubulovillous_present.definition: At least one adenoma has villous or tubulovillous histology.

current_polyp_dysplasia_grade.definition: Highest dysplasia grade reported for a polyp found at the current examination.

high_grade_dysplasia_stated.definition: The case explicitly states that high-grade dysplasia is present in a polyp found at the current examination.

ssp_ssl_dysplasia_present.definition: At least one SSP/SSL shows dysplasia.

malignant_polyp_present.definition: A polyp with malignant (invasive) histology is found.

ctdna_test_result.definition: Result of blood-based circulating tumor DNA testing.

lesion_resectable.definition: Clinician judgement that the lesion can be removed endoscopically (resectable).

endoscopic_resection_status.definition: Status of endoscopic resection of the lesion.

lesion_size_mm.definition: Size of the resected lesion, in mm.

active_inflammation_present.definition: Endoscopic or histologic active inflammation is present.

family_history_crc_diagnosed_before_50.definition: A relative has CRC diagnosed before age 50.

stricture_traversable.definition: The colon stricture can be traversed by the endoscope.

chromoendoscopy_performed.definition: Chromoendoscopy (dye spray or high-definition virtual) with targeted biopsies was performed.

gi_pathology_review_result.definition: Result of GI pathologist review of biopsies.

family_history_positive.definition: Positive family history of CRC or advanced neoplasia in a relative.

first_degree_relative_high_grade_dysplas.definition: A polyp in a first-degree relative shows high-grade dysplasia. The boxes state no criteria and name no standard definition, so the reported pathology grade is used; a case that explicitly states high-grade dysplasia is accepted.

first_degree_relative_advanced_neoplasia.definition: A first-degree relative has a confirmed advanced adenoma or advanced SSP/SSL (size at least 1 cm, villous or tubulovillous or TSA histology, or high-grade dysplasia).

high_grade_dysplasia_present.definition: High-grade dysplasia is present in a polyp found at the current examination. The boxes state no criteria and name no standard definition, so the reported pathology grade is used; a case that explicitly states high-grade dysplasia is accepted.

personal_history_polyp_from_findings.definition: Personal history of adenoma(s), SSP/SSL(s), traditional serrated adenoma(s) (TSA), or a large (at least 1 cm) hyperplastic polyp found at colonoscopy.

therapy_associated_polyposis.definition: Patient meets criteria for therapy-associated polyposis after childhood, adolescent, or young adult cancer.

polypectomy_category.definition: Category of polyps removed at polypectomy, used to choose the next surveillance step.

index_polyp_risk.definition: Risk category of polyps found at a personal-history colonoscopy.

ibd_surveillance_risk.definition: Risk category for colitis (IBD) surveillance after dysplasia-free or invisible-dysplasia findings.

resected_lesion_risk.definition: Risk category of a resected lesion in colitis surveillance, based on histology, size and clinical factors.

notes.predicates: Conditions were drafted and reviewed by a language model (model_reviewed), not by clinicians. 'rejected' means the review rejected the draft; the box then needs clinician judgement. 'section_only' means the box only requires the patient to be in the page's guideline section.
notes.coordinates: bbox and line_bboxes are PDF points with the origin at the page's top left; pages[].size gives the page size.
notes.links: page links name a page id from pages[]; a multi-page code such as PROS-F has ids 'PROS-F 1 of 5' ... ; external_guideline links name another guideline's slug.
